messages:
maya: quick sweep ahead of tomorrow's shiproom — we have 3 open models to clear: riptide-7b (ajay), glade-2.1-6b (leah), nettle-13b (samir). need: (1) explicit license compatibility callout, (2) perf profile (p50/p95 tokens @ typical seq), (3) canary plan + rollback gating. pinging eng-platform & legal. any blockers?

ajay: riptide license looks permissive but there's a data-derived clause in the model card. i flagged it to legal. perf quick numbers from my local perf harness:
```
model: riptide-7b
seq=512, batch=8 -> p50 token=14ms, p95 token=38ms
quantized (4-bit) -> p50=9ms, p95=29ms
```
I'll run the full nightly suite tonight, but those are the ballpark numbers. canary plan: canary-group: 2% traffic -> fallback to riptide-4b if latency > 60ms.

leah: glade-2.1-6b model card is marked CC-BY-SA with a separate dataset license note. initial read seems OK for hosting but NOT for repackaging. legal: can you confirm CC-BY-SA implications for our hosted API?

samir: nettle-13b I'm still waiting on tokenizer mapping fix in the ingest pipeline — blocked on a small mapping PR (eng-platform review requested). perf wise i have a rough baseline: p50 token ~= 24ms at seq=1024 (batch=4). ETA to run full bench: EOD my timezone.

miranda (legal): quick answers:
- riptide: data-derived clause needs review; if the clause restricts commercial use of derivative outputs we can't list it as hosted-for-sale. can ajay paste the exact clause (or link) here?
- glade (CC-BY-SA): CC-BY-SA is a share-alike license. hosting as a public inference endpoint is typically fine, but if we redistribute model weights (or create a repackaged derivative) that's when SA triggers. please confirm whether we plan to distribute weights or only provide API access.
- nettle: no immediate red flags on the license text you pasted earlier, but i need the final model attribution and data provenance fields filled in the intake form.

ajay: pasted the riptide clause — see snippet: "models trained on proprietary third-party corpora must obtain explicit commercial permissions". i think it's the third-party corpora part that trips us. linking intake: https://intranet.redwood/models/riptide-7b

leah: we will only expose as API (no weight distribution) for glade. that's the current plan.

ops-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: canary/riptide-7b/2024-11-07 02:00 UTC -> 2% traffic. monitor: latency, error-rate, hallucination-rate. rollback policy: 3 consecutive 5-min windows over p95>80ms or error-rate>1%.

samir: PR for tokenizer mapping is out, added @eng-platform for review. small test vector included. once merged I'll run the bench and post numbers.

maya: thanks — action items summary:
- ajay: paste full riptide clause + run full nightly bench (due: tonight)
- leah: confirm intake fields (distribution=no) and post final model card link
- samir: get eng-platform review on tokenizer PR and post bench numbers (ETA EOD)
- miranda/legal: final license go/no-go on riptide after clause review
- eng-platform: quick review of nettle tokenizer PR + confirm canary config okay
I'll fold this into the shiproom doc and pin before the 9am sync. doc: https://docs.redwood/shiproom/model-catalog-launch (will update after benches). :thumbsup:

ajay: noted. will update the doc and call out quantization numbers too.

leah: putting final model-card link in the intake form now.

miranda (legal): reading the full clause now, should have a call by EOD if anything is blocking.

maya: perfect. if anything blocks shiproom we escalate to product + eng-vp. otherwise see you in the 9am slot.
